summary.text: 差 is used for difference, mismatch, and unevenness, among other distinct reading-and-sense groups. Its received traditional analysis explains it as mismatch, but early bronze forms have competing interpretations, so no single origin is secure.

formation.text: The received Shuowen account analyzes 差 as 从左从𠂹, relating it to mismatch. A modern paleographic proposal instead distinguishes bronze form groups: one may depict bundled fuel and relate to 㷢, while another may show misaligned hands with 左 as a phonetic note. These are competing interpretations, not a demonstrated sequence. The popular account of wheat rubbed between hands is disputed and unsupported as an identification of the early graph.

components.text: In the received Shuowen analysis, 左 is one of two parts in 差. A separate paleographic proposal treats 左 as a phonetic note in one distinct ancient form; it does not establish that all early 差 forms contained the complete 左 graph. 左 itself developed from a left-hand pictograph 𠂇 with 工 added in later bronze forms. This history belongs to 左 and cannot settle 差’s internal structure.

sound.text: For the proposed phonetic role in one ancient 差 form, Baxter–Sagart reconstructs 左 *tsˤa[j]ʔ and 差 chā *tsʰraj in Old Chinese. The initial consonants differ, so this is a related sound-series proposal rather than an identical reading; the evidence does not establish this role across all 差 forms.

components.text: 𠂹 is the second part in the received Shuowen analysis, where the whole graph is glossed as mismatch. A later lexicographic interpretation associates it with divergence. The dossier does not establish an independent lexical or pictorial function for this form in 差, nor a separate earlier form for it.

In one proposed analysis of a separate ancient form, the lower structure is interpreted as two hands out of alignment. This is an interpretation of an early form, not an established component of the modern graph or of every ancient 差 form; the dossier does not specify a canonical Han component for those hands.

history.text: The curated Western Zhou bronze-style image is a modern redraw associated with 同簋蓋, not an artifact photograph. The recorded early bronze forms are debated, and the specialist account reports no oracle-bone 差 in the materials it considered; these facts do not establish a linear development into the modern graph.

The received Shuowen account analyzes 差 as 左 plus 𠂹 and glosses it as mismatch. Later annotation discusses mismatch, divergence, unevenness, and selection, but this lexicographic interpretation does not directly confirm the earliest graphic form.

A separate modern proposal connects a form interpreted as bundled fuel with 㷢, whose gloss is ‘bundle of charcoal’; the cited bronze use of 㷢 is loanwise for 差. The proposal that the early 差 picture named that fuel is tentative, and its spoken name and pronunciation are not independently known, so the proposed borrowing mechanism cannot be verified by a sound comparison.

uncertainties.text: The wheat-rubbing account identifies upper shapes as 來 and a hand, but specialist paleographic analysis disputes that reading; the resemblance of a part to 來 or 羊 does not establish its identity in 差.

Early bronze forms have more than one proposed analysis, and some forms have also been read as 樹. Neither the traditional Shuowen analysis nor the modern bundled-fuel and misaligned-hands proposals establishes one origin for every form and reading.

Pronunciation reconstructions are reading-specific and system-specific. The proposed 左 phonetic relation is not a simple identity of sound, and the dossier does not establish that it applies across all 差 readings.

Textual evidence supports uses for selecting, unevenness, mismatch or error, and a ritual washing verb, but does not establish a complete chronology or semantic path among these senses. The composition dates of the cited Odes and Xunzi passages are unresolved here.

senses.period: Han lexicographic account; graph attested in Western Zhou bronzes
senses.text: The received Shuowen gloss and analysis record 差 as mismatch. This establishes a historical lexicographic interpretation, not necessarily the earliest spoken meaning.

senses.period: early textual use; precise composition date unresolved
senses.text: In the transmitted Odes passage ‘既差我馬,’ traditional lexicography reads 差 as selecting the horses. This is an early attested use, not proof that selection was the word’s original meaning.

senses.period: early compound use; precise dating unresolved
senses.text: The compound 參差 is attested in an Odes line and glossed as uneven or irregular. This attests the compound meaning but does not date the standalone sense or show its development from mismatch.
Modern dictionaries group difference and distinction among the character’s senses. The dossier does not establish when these developed from, or became associated with, mismatch.

senses.period: historical and current; earliest dating unresolved
senses.text: Error and discrepancy are recorded senses. A pre-imperial Xunzi passage contains 差 in a divergence- or error-related context, though its precise nuance is uncertain.

senses.period: historical and current; earliest dating unresolved
senses.text: A distinct reading tradition has the senses select, dispatch, or a dispatched person/task. The evidence lists these senses but does not establish their semantic path from mismatch or difference.
A ritual passage uses 差 for rinsing, glossed as rice-washing. It is a distinct reading and lexical use; the evidence does not connect it to difference or to the proposed wheat-rubbing origin.

senses.period: historical and current through the spelling 瘥; dating unresolved
senses.text: A separate reading tradition records recovery, later also written 瘥. The dossier supplies no supported semantic transition linking it to the other senses.

developments.text: Later lexicographic interpretation associates mismatch and divergence with unevenness, but the available evidence does not establish a historical transition between them.
The meanings are related in lexicographic explanation and textual interpretation, but the dossier does not establish when or how error developed from mismatch.

limitations.text: The listed modern and historical senses do not by themselves establish chronology. Dates of the cited textual compositions are unresolved, and several reading groups have no supported transition connecting them.

A tentative graph-borrowing proposal links a pictured fuel bundle to 㷢, but the bundle’s ancient spoken name and pronunciation are unverified; no sound comparison can confirm why its graph was reused for 差.

overview.text: 差 commonly expresses difference, mismatch, or unevenness. Its traditional analysis links the graph to mismatch, while early bronze forms also have competing interpretations; the popular wheat-rubbing explanation is disputed.

components.text: 左 appears in the traditional account and is proposed as a sound note in one distinct early form; that proposal does not describe every form of 差.
𠂹 is the second part in the traditional account, interpreted in later annotation in connection with mismatch and divergence.
A competing early-form analysis sees two misaligned hands, but does not establish them as parts of the modern graph.

relationships.text: One paleographic analysis proposes 左 as a phonetic note in a distinct ancient 差 form; the claim is form-specific and does not establish the same role in every form.
A competing analysis interprets the lower structure in one distinct ancient form as two misaligned hands; this is not a claim that modern 差 contains 𠂇 as a component.
